title: fix(app-shell): derive the CEL placeholder from the roots a mount offers
body:
Fixes #9952

## 0. Re-taken readings — the card body's line numbers are stale, none of them is cited here

A point-in-time **receipt**, taken by me on my own base, objectui `origin/main` `1db82373f767c5331d7ce8d1bfb9beb4420f7cf5` (the same tip the dispatch named). Every number below is a reading of one file, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ConditionBuilder.tsx`, named once here so the numbers are not a cross-file address. Per AGENTS.md #11 they are **not** carried into the code, the tests or the changeset — those cite by symbol name and quoted text only, and `pnpm check:new-line-citations` prints `0 new citation(s)` on this branch.

| reading | the card body says | what I read on `1db82373f` |
|---|---|---|
| `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS = ['record', 'previous'];` | `:195` | **`:242`** |
| the CEL example placeholder, a string literal | `:479` | **`:566`** — text unchanged |
| CONTROL — `roots` lines in the file | 16 | **18** |
| CONTROL — `placeholder=` sites in the file | 3 | **3** — the other two are `:618` (`field / context`, a `SelectValue`) and `:642` (`value`, an `Input`), both unrelated, so the CEL example was the only one |

The two controls are what make the placeholder's absence from the roots machinery a reading rather than a failed search.

## 1. Both relayed claims re-measured — both reproduce

The dispatch marked two load-bearing facts as relayed and ordered them re-measured before a line of fix.

**Claim A — objectstack's hook wrapper binds two names.** Read at source in `packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`, in the `wrapDeclarativeHook` docblock, on the objectstack checkout at `0b31d90f`. Verbatim:

> The condition formula is evaluated against two bindings, the same two a validation predicate reads (#4784):
>
>   - `record`   — the record-shaped view built by {@link pickRecordPayload} …
>   - `previous` — the record's pre-write state, built by {@link pickPreviousPayload} …

No `user`, no `org`. ⇒ **reproduces.** At a server-evaluated mount the taught root is unbound, not merely unadvertised.

**Claim B — objectui's own `conditionScope.ts` says the same thing from this side.** Read on my base, in the ruling bullets and again in the `validation` row's docblock. Verbatim:

> validation rule `condition` → `record`: objectql's rule validator binds `{ record, previous }` and fail-closes on an unevaluable predicate, so a bare reference rejects every write to the object.

> hook `condition` → `record`: `wrapDeclarativeHook` evaluates it as `{ record: record ?? {}, previous }` and throws on an unevaluable one.

> a validation rule's `condition` is evaluated by objectql's rule validator with `{ record, previous }` and nothing else, and an unevaluable predicate there is fail-CLOSED

⇒ **reproduces**, including the fail-CLOSED half. ⚠️ One correction to the relay, offered as a reading and not as a re-opening: triage cited this as `conditionScope.ts:83-120`. On my base the sentences sit in the ruling bullet list near the top of the file and in the `validation` key's own docblock; `83-120` opens at the `CONDITION_SCOPE_BY_METADATA_TYPE` declaration and covers only the second of the two. The substance is unchanged.

**Counter-fact, also re-measured.** `@objectstack/formula`'s `introspectScope('predicate', …)` advertises `["record","previous","input","os","current_user","user","vars"]` at BOTH `record` and `flattened` scope, and `SCOPE_ROOTS` carries `user`. ⇒ `user.isAdmin` is right at a client-evaluated mount and unbound at a server-evaluated one — exactly what one literal cannot express, and the reason this PR narrows nothing anywhere else.

## 2. The route — A and B collapsed into one, because the bar forbids the second list

Route **A** (parameterise by `scope`) and route **B** (derive from the mount's own declared subjects) are the same edit here, once the offered set is read only once:

```tsx
const offeredRoots = roots ?? (scope === 'record' ? RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS : undefined);
…
placeholder={celExampleForRoots(offeredRoots)}
roots={offeredRoots}
```

That expression was already in the JSX as the `roots` value; hoisting it makes **one value** answer both controls, so the two cannot disagree by construction.

`celExampleForRoots` takes a list of example **clauses** and keeps a clause only when every root it SPELLS is in the offered set. The roots are read back out of each clause's own text by `celRootsMentioned` — so there is no per-scope table, and no list of roots tagged onto the clauses that someone could edit out of step. A clause referencing an unoffered root **disappears**; it cannot mis-teach it. This is what the bar asked for: ⛔ no second hand-maintained list, which is how the autocomplete (objectui#9645), the subject dropdown (objectui#9855) and this placeholder got out of step one control at a time.

⛔ Route **C** (drop the second clause) was rejected: it would take `user.isAdmin` away from the client-evaluated mounts where `buildExpressionScope` really does bind it — the very thing the card says this is not.

**Nothing is removed.** `undefined` offered roots means the mount declared no narrowing and inherits the engine's own advertisement, which carries `user`; every clause survives and that placeholder is byte-identical to what it was. Only TEACHING narrows — the accept set and the subject dropdown are untouched.

## 3. Tests — the relation, and the proof the instrument can fail

`ConditionBuilder.placeholderRoots.test.tsx`, 13 cases. ⛔ No case asserts what the placeholder SAYS. Each reads the real `placeholder` attribute off the rendered editor and asserts every root in it is a member of the set that mount offers.

- **subject** — a `scope="record"` mount mentions no root outside `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS`; plus a case that it still teaches SOMETHING, so an emptied placeholder cannot pass the first one.
- **control A — the instrument can FAIL** — the OLD literal is fed to the same relation against the same offered set and must be REJECTED, naming `user`; a second case feeds it an all-offered example and requires acceptance, so it is not a rejector that rejects everything.
- **control B — nothing is lost** — a mount with no `scope` still teaches `record` and `user`; every root it teaches is one `introspectCelScope` itself advertises (both sides derived, so an engine that stops advertising one reddens here); and a mount that DECLARES `roots` gets those clauses taught again.
- the derivation quantified over the power set of the roots the shipped clauses mention plus one the component never offers, and the extractor's own edges (a quoted `'user.id'` is text, a dotted member is not a root, `true` / `null` are not roots).

### Failing-control evidence — a one-shot ablation, on disk, restored

The in-body control A proves the ASSERTION can fail. This proves the FILE is really what makes it pass. The fix was committed first, then the JSX placeholder mutated back to the literal, the mutation verified on disk by text counts and by blob hash, and the restore verified the same way.


Both legs ran against SOURCE — these tests import `./ConditionBuilder` relatively, so no `dist` sits between the mutation and the run. The mutation script carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restoring by `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`, and the restore is proven by the blob hash and by an empty `git diff HEAD`, never by an exit code. ⛔ Nothing from this ablation is left in the tree.

## 4. Checks run

| check | verdict |
|---|---|
| the 8 `ConditionBuilder.*` suites (7 existing + the new one) | `Test Files 8 passed (8)` · `Tests 91 passed (91)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`), after building the package's dependency closure | exit 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` · `check:new-line-citations` · `check:vi-mock-specifiers` · `check:vi-mock-inherit` · `check:vi-mock-override-shape` · `check:test-path-roots` · `check:pending-changeset-literals` · `check:changeset-claims` · `check:unreferenced-sources` · `check:i18n-keys` · `changeset:check` | all exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | OK — 1 source file of 1 released package, 1 changeset declared |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test …` | NOT GOVERNED — 3 paths, none matched |
| `check:readme-exports` | **NOT MEASURED** — exit 1 is `type entry ./dist/index.d.ts is not on disk — run pnpm build first` for 86 self-imports across app-shell, cli, plugin-ai, plugin-gantt and others; a prerequisite, not a finding. Only app-shell's dependency closure was built locally. Nothing here touches a README, and `ConditionBuilder` is not on the package's public entry, so the new exports add no README claim. |

### Lint — a declared narrowing, with its three readings

`eslint .` repo-wide is CI's run. Locally I linted only the two changed sources, and the narrowing is a measurement rather than a skip:

1. **population** — read from `eslint.config.js` itself: `**/*.{ts,tsx}` under its `ignores` (`dist`, `.next`, `node_modules`, `public`, `.source`, plus three literal generated paths), which is 4992 tracked files.
2. **files linted** — `2`, read from `--format json`'s own output.
3. **invariance** — `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off ⇒ this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.

Result: **0 errors** on both files. `ConditionBuilder.tsx` carries **6 warnings**, against **4** on the base — the delta is 2 × `react-refresh/only-export-components`, one for each new export. Declared rather than hidden: that file already trades this warning for its three existing non-component exports (`REFERENCE_ROOTS`, `RECORD_CONDITION_ROOTS`, `RECORD_CONDITION_SUBJECTS`), which the sibling pins read the same way the new pin reads these two. Moving the helpers to a new module would silence it, at the cost of a file outside this card's declared face.

## 5. Scope

Touched: the component, one new sibling pin, one changeset. ⛔ `ConditionWidget` / objectui#9953 untouched — a different subject, as the claim ruled. ⛔ objectui#9645 and objectui#9855's landed work is neither re-opened nor re-worded; their docblocks are cited, not edited. ⛔ Nothing in objectstack, and no engine root set moved: `SCOPE_ROOTS` and `buildExpressionScope` were READ to re-measure the counter-fact and are otherwise untouched.

⚠️ One declared deviation from the dispatch's file face. The pin landed at `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ConditionBuilder.placeholderRoots.test.tsx`, beside its six `ConditionBuilder.*.test.tsx` siblings, rather than under `inspectors/__tests__/`. That directory exists but holds no `ConditionBuilder` test; the claim named the exact path as the dev's, and the repo's own convention for this component is colocation.

Draft on purpose. ⛔ Not ready for review, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ not merged — landing is the `domain:ui#2` seat's act.
